paragraphs: Children in care in Stockton-on-Tees are looked after by Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council's own fostering service, shown above alongside the independent agencies that cover the borough. The council is looking for people from all walks of life to care for babies, younger children, teenagers and brothers and sisters who need to stay together, in arrangements ranging from short breaks and short-term care to long-term fostering.

Stockton belongs to Foster with North East, a regional partnership of twelve councils led by Together for Children, which runs children's services for Sunderland. The hub is the first point of contact: it sends out an information pack and guides people through the early stages, while the assessment, approval and day-to-day support stay with Stockton's own fostering team. The council's page lists free online information evenings, including one on 30 November 2026 from 6pm to 7pm.

To apply to the council you normally need to be 25 or over, though people aged 21 to 25 can be considered in some cases. You need a spare bedroom for a foster child (a baby can sleep in a cot in your room), you must live in the UK full time or have leave to remain, and you need the time to care for a child, often on a full-time basis.

Every council carer has a supervising social worker in the Children's Fostering and Carers Team who helps with training and development. The council's support page gives a weekly allowance per child of £150 to £255 for newer carers and £275 to £380 for experienced carers, depending on the child's age, plus extra payments for birthdays and holidays. The page carries no date, so ask the team to confirm current rates. The minimum the government sets for 2026-27 outside London and the South East runs from £176 a week for a baby to £267 for a 16 or 17 year old.
A good first step is to speak to two or three of the services above and compare their training, support and how they match children with carers.
